ann_33.original: Additive risk terms. Each input on this leaf adds its own edge weight times its z-score to the logit, with no interaction between them. The largest direct terms are the number of major vessels seen on fluoroscopy (ca, 1.51 per sd), female sex (-1.08 per sd of the female indicator) and an upsloping ST segment (-0.90 per sd). Cholesterol (0.53), resting blood pressure (0.49), asymptomatic chest pain (0.33) and exercise angina (0.43) raise the score directly; typical angina (-0.53), non-anginal pain (-0.47) and a normal thallium scan (-0.43) lower it. Age, non-anginal pain, resting blood pressure, a normal resting ECG and the fixed and reversible thal levels also feed the hidden nodes, so for them this direct term is not the whole-model effect (see the hinge and gate parts). Prediction and self-probe, typical patient in the whole model: predicted risk rises with each extra vessel for both sexes and women sit lower at every count, from 2% for a woman and 19% for a man with no vessels to 80% and 97% with three. Switching this leaf off (its mean kept) drops training AUC from 0.942 to 0.766, the largest loss of any part. The full linear sum is attached as the analytical formula.
ann_33.proposed: Each input adds its own amount to the predicted risk: more vessels coloured by fluoroscopy raise it steadily, and being a woman or having typical angina lowers it.

ann_34.original: 204 ≈ relu(2.55·oldpeak + 0.937·restecg0 + 1.13·thal7 + 0.276), in z-scores (off by up to 0.022 from rounding). An exercise-ischaemia score: it switches on with ST depression on exercise (oldpeak), and a reversible thallium defect switches it on earlier and higher. It is on for 117 of 242 training patients, whose outcome rate is 65.8% against 24.0% for the 125 where it is off. For the 117 it acts on it adds 0.84 to the logit on average in the whole model, through its own output edge (weight 0.117) and through the gate 290 (weight 1.09). It is on for all 47 patients with oldpeak of 2 mm or more (share 100%). Self-probe, typical patient: with a normal scan it is off at 0.5 mm of ST depression (0.00) and on at 1 mm (0.26); with a reversible defect it is already on at 0 mm (0.45), and predicted risk at 2 mm is 72% against 30% with a normal scan. With oldpeak at 0 it is on for 7 patients, a small regime. Of the 90 patients with a reversible defect, 78 have it on. Unexpected direction: a normal resting ECG raises this score (at 1 mm, 0.26 with a normal ECG and 0.00 with left ventricular hypertrophy), although whole-model risk is still higher with hypertrophy (26% against 20%) because of the direct resting-ECG edge. Switching it off lowers training AUC from 0.942 to 0.932.
ann_34.proposed: ST depression on exercise adds to the predicted risk once it rises above about 0.9 mm, slowly at first, then faster, but for 88 of the 242 training patients it already acts below that: for a typical such patient, going from 0.0 mm to 3.5 mm moves the risk from about 26% to about 53%. A reversible defect on the thallium scan raises the predicted risk, and even more so if the resting ECG is normal: for a typical patient, from about 19% to about 44% with a normal resting ECG and from about 26% to about 43% with any other resting ECG.

ann_35.original: 2116 ≈ relu(1.0·relu(1.0·thal6 + 2.12) + 0.0355), in z-scores (off by up to 0.02 from rounding). Both relays are on for all 242 training rows (share 100%), so the chain passes the fixed-defect indicator plus a constant to the gate 290, where it enters with weight -0.0132. Described, not explained: it carries no behaviour beyond a very small push on the gate for the 15 patients with a fixed defect. Self-probe, typical patient: going from a normal scan to a fixed defect raises 2116 from 1.91 to 6.07, and the gate's input moves from -0.499 to -0.363, mostly from the direct thal edge into the gate, not from this chain. ann_35.proposed: This small relay passes the fixed-defect result of the thallium scan to the gate above and barely changes the predictions.

ann_36.original: A blood-pressure gate on the ischaemia score. Node 290 is a ReLU that adds the ST-depression hinge (weight 1.09) to resting blood pressure with a negative weight (-0.82 per sd), plus small atypical-angina (0.151), fixed-defect (0.046) and non-anginal-pain (0.017) terms and the thal relay chain. It is on for 135 of 242 patients, 100 of them with the hinge on; for 35 it is on with the hinge off, opened by low blood pressure, and their outcome rate is 20.0%. The gate adds risk, so for patients with ST depression a lower blood pressure is given extra risk here while a higher one is given risk by its direct edge: the whole-model blood-pressure slope is flatter for them. Self-probe, typical patient with oldpeak 2 mm: from 100 to 180 mm Hg the gate falls from 3.48 to 0.00 and the score rises from -1.24 to 0.21; with oldpeak 0 the score rises more steeply, from -2.15 to -0.07. For the 152 patients this part acts on it adds 0.67 to the logit on average in the whole model. Switching it off lowers training AUC from 0.942 to 0.932.
ann_36.proposed: This gate adds to the predicted risk once ST depression on exercise rises above about 0.9 mm, slowly at first, then faster, though for 88 of the 242 training patients it already acts below that. Higher ST depression on exercise raises the predicted risk of heart disease, and even more so if the thallium scan shows a reversible defect: for a typical patient, going from 0.0 mm to 2.8 mm moves it from about 35% to about 84% with a reversible defect and from about 19% to about 48% with neither a fixed nor a reversible defect; for most patients with a reversible defect it rises slowly at first, then faster, but for some of them with a normal resting ECG (17 of the 44 sampled) it rises steadily.

ann_37.original: How the gate reaches the output: its own edge (weight 0.135), the hinge 1834, which adds extra risk once the gate is large (gate weight 0.94, output weight 0.165), and the age hinge 1987, which gives older patients a little extra risk while the gate is off (age weight 0.88 per sd, gate weight -1.58, output weight 0.097); the three are added to the logit. 1834 is on for 63 patients, whose outcome rate is 77.8%; 1987 is on for 85. Self-probe, typical patient: with oldpeak 0 the age hinge is off at 50 years (0.00) and on at 60 and 70 (0.68, 1.65); with oldpeak 2 mm the gate is on (2.13) and the age hinge is off at 70 (0.00), so risk rises less with age there (26% to 34% from 40 to 70, against 16% to 25% with oldpeak 0, in logit terms a flatter slope). With oldpeak 2 mm, 1834 is on at 100 mm Hg (1.61) and off at 140 (0.00). For the 206 patients this part acts on it adds 0.54 to the logit on average in the whole model; switching it off lowers training AUC from 0.942 to 0.932.
ann_37.proposed: This part adds to the predicted risk once ST depression on exercise rises above about 0.9 mm, slowly at first, then faster, though for 88 of the 242 training patients it already acts below that. It also adds a little for age, with nothing until about 53 years (between 53 years and 66 years for different patients), then steadily.

ann_38.original: Predicted risk is the sigmoid of the sum of the direct linear terms, the gate readouts and the output bias: the parts are added on the logit scale, and the nonlinear part acts on the ischaemia and blood-pressure side. The inputs sex:1, fbs:1, restecg:1, restecg:2, slope:2 and thal:4 have no edge in the model (their levels are carried by the other indicator of the same variable). The model reproduces the network to 2.2e-16 on the training rows. Self-probe, whole model: for the typical male patient, ST depression raises predicted risk from 19% at 0 mm to 53% at 3 mm with a normal scan and from 35% to 87% with a reversible defect, and more vessels raise it from 19% to 97% (none to three). The direct terms carry most of the ranking (AUC 0.766 without them against 0.942 with them); the gate readouts add 0.54 to the logit on average for the 206 patients they act on.
ann_38.proposed: The model adds up two parts: a sum in which each input counts on its own, and a part built on ST depression on exercise that the thallium scan, the resting ECG and age adjust. Each extra vessel coloured by fluoroscopy raises the predicted risk steadily, a flat ST segment raises it, and ST depression on exercise raises it slowly at first, then faster: for a typical patient, from about 19% to about 88% (0 vessels to 2 vessels), to about 59%, and to about 48% (0.0 mm to 2.8 mm). Being a woman, typical angina and non-anginal chest pain lower it, for a typical patient to about 2%, 2% and 4%.

parts.name: direct_linear_terms
parts.original_hypothesis: Additive risk terms. Each input on this leaf adds its own edge weight times its z-score to the logit, with no interaction between them. The largest direct terms are the number of major vessels seen on fluoroscopy (ca, 1.51 per sd), female sex (-1.08 per sd of the female indicator) and an upsloping ST segment (-0.90 per sd). Cholesterol (0.53), resting blood pressure (0.49), asymptomatic chest pain (0.33) and exercise angina (0.43) raise the score directly; typical angina (-0.53), non-anginal pain (-0.47) and a normal thallium scan (-0.43) lower it. Age, non-anginal pain, resting blood pressure, a normal resting ECG and the fixed and reversible thal levels also feed the hidden nodes, so for them this direct term is not the whole-model effect (see the hinge and gate parts). Prediction and self-probe, typical patient in the whole model: predicted risk rises with each extra vessel for both sexes and women sit lower at every count, from 2% for a woman and 19% for a man with no vessels to 80% and 97% with three. Switching this leaf off (its mean kept) drops training AUC from 0.942 to 0.766, the largest loss of any part. The full linear sum is attached as the analytical formula.

summary.text: The model treats a higher number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy as raising the predicted risk of heart disease steadily, each extra vessel adding about the same: for a typical patient, it goes from about 19% at 0 vessels to about 88% at 2 vessels, flattening out near the top because the predicted risk cannot go much higher (on the training data only).

The model treats a higher ST depression on exercise as raising the predicted risk of heart disease slowly at first, then faster: for a typical patient, it goes from about 19% at 0.0 mm to about 48% at 2.8 mm (on the training data only).

Through one part of the model, ST depression on exercise adds to the predicted risk of heart disease once it rises above about 0.9 mm (for 88 of the 242 training patients it already changes below that): for a typical such patient, going from 0.0 mm to 3.5 mm moves it from about 26% to about 53% (on the training data only).

The model gives a clearly higher predicted risk of heart disease if the thallium scan shows a reversible defect than if thallium stress test result is something other than a reversible defect on the thallium scan, and even more so if the resting ECG is normal: for a typical patient, going from thallium stress test result other than a reversible defect on the thallium scan to a reversible defect on the thallium scan moves the predicted risk of heart disease from about 19% to about 44% if the resting ECG is normal, and from about 26% to about 43% if resting ECG is something other than a normal resting ECG.
